X.finding: A live-looking API key is committed to git
X.why: application.yml:7 holds api-key: claims-prod-9f2c4e1a7b3d8e60; report names the key in the repo, the history problem and env-based fix.

X.finding: The model's answer starts a payment, with no adjuster in between
X.why: TriageService.java:66-67 pays result.amountClaimed()/currency on APPROVE with no check; application.yml:9 auto-approve: true; both cited correctly.

X.finding: The claimant's email is pasted into the system prompt
X.why: TriageService.java:36-41 concatenates email into the text passed to .system(prompt) at :51; report states the injection payload and what the attacker gets.

X.finding: Stored and reflected XSS on the adjuster page
X.why: ClaimsController.java:39 and :41 build text/html by concatenating claimId and r.summary() unescaped; both sources named.

X.finding: temperature(0.0) on Haiku 5.5 is rejected with a 400 and the retry loop hides it
X.why: TriageService.java:50 sets temperature(0.0) on claude-haiku-5-5; report explicitly says the request is rejected with a 400 for this model and that the :58 catch swallows it; bare 500 from :63 is also correct.

X.finding: Full claim email and model answer go to the info log
X.why: TriageService.java:56 logs prompt (with email) and answer at INFO; report also cites :59 e.getMessage().

X.finding: Answer read before the stop reason is checked (refusal / max_tokens)
X.why: TriageService.java:55 reads content().get(0).text().get() with no stopReason() check; report names refusal, max_tokens cut-off with 512 tokens and NoSuchElementException.

X.finding: Client built on every attempt, no timeout
X.why: TriageService.java:46 builds AnthropicOkHttpClient inside the 5-attempt loop with defaults and no timeout; report names both the per-attempt client/pool and the missing timeout.
TriageResult.java:4 amountClaimed and PaymentService.java:16,20 amount are double; cited.

X.finding: pay is not idempotent: the same claimId POSTed twice is paid twice
X.why: ClaimsController.triage (:27-31) always calls triage.triage, which pays on every APPROVE for the same claimId; PaymentService.pay just appends. A double payout is a money bug not in the key.

X.finding: ClaimRequest.email has no @NotBlank/@Size, so an empty or 5 MB email goes to the paid API
X.why: ClaimsController.java:18 record has no constraints and :28 has no @Valid although spring-boot-starter-validation is in the pom; unbounded input to the model named.

X.finding: Jackson 2 ObjectMapper import alongside Boot 4 (hidden dependency)
X.why: TriageService.java:7 does import com.fasterxml; this is on the answer key's Not-defects list, and the report hedges it as 'possible'.

X.finding: Results store lives in the controller (controller -> service)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:21 holds the ConcurrentHashMap; in-memory demo storage is a Not-defect and the layering point is an opinion ('possible divergent change').

X.finding: No authorization on a page that shows claimants' personal data
X.why: ClaimsController.java:35 has no auth and there is no security starter in the pom, so the page is open; report itself downgrades it to 'probably fine for a demo' and covers only the page, not the triage POST.

X.finding: No tests for refusal, cut-off, unparseable and APPROVE-but-don't-pay cases
X.why: No tests is on the answer key's Not-defects list (fixture deliberately small).

Y.finding: Claim email can trigger a payment (email in the system prompt)
Y.why: TriageService.java:36-41 pastes the public email into the system prompt; report gives the injection example and the attacker-chosen amount.

Y.finding: Claim email can trigger a payment (model decides instead of an adjuster, auto-approve)
Y.why: TriageService.java:66-68 pays the model's amount/currency on APPROVE, switched on by application.yml:9; cites CLAUDE.md 'adjusters decide'.

Y.finding: A real-looking API key is committed to config
Y.why: application.yml:7 hard-codes the key; report says env/secret store and notes git history and rotation.

Y.finding: Stored XSS on the adjuster page
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:39 and :41 concatenate r.summary() and claimId into text/html unescaped; both named.
Same claimId POSTed again re-runs triage and appends a second Payment (ClaimsController.java:27-31, TriageService.java:66-68); a double payout is a money bug not in the key.

Y.finding: No authentication or per-claim authorization; anyone can triage or read any summary
Y.why: No security starter in the pom and no checks in ClaimsController, so any caller can trigger triage (a paid API call and possibly a payment) or read claimants' summaries.
TriageService.java:56 logs the whole prompt (email) and the answer (claimantName) at INFO; the :59 e.getMessage() point is not needed for full.

Y.finding: Retry loop: broad catch, new client per attempt, no timeout
Y.why: TriageService.java:44-61 builds a new AnthropicOkHttpClient per attempt, never closes it, sets no timeout; also correctly notes the catch retries a 401 and parse errors and drops the cause.

Y.finding: No input validation and no clear error response
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:18 and :28 have no constraints or @Valid; null or multi-MB email goes to the model (cost); validation starter unused.

Y.finding: amountClaimed stored as a double (and negative amount not checked)
Y.why: TriageResult.java:4 double amountClaimed; PaymentService also double. Negative-amount remark is true but minor.
TriageService.java:7 is on the answer key's Not-defects list; report hedges with 'probably'.

Y.finding: content().get(0).text().get() throws if the first block isn't text
